To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

melatonin disappears rapidly from the brain, that the disappearance of melatonin is faster in constant light than in constant darkness and that the disappearance is faster in constant darkness than in the dark:light cycle.

melatonin injected intracisternally into rats disappears rapidly from the brain, that the disappearance of melatonin from the brain exhibits at least 2 exponential components, and that the disappearance rate of intracisternal melatonin is influenced by light exposure.

1) the disappearance of 14C-melatonin from rat brain after its intracisternal injection is a 2-component process; 2) the half-lives of these 2 components are 2–5 min and 40–60 min, respectively; and 3) the concentration of melatonin is 3–5 times higher in the hypothalamo-pituitary region of the brain than in the rest of it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the turnover of 3-hydroxytryptamine and its metabolites in the brain.
the fate of melatonin after its intracisternal injection into the brain.
the turnover of intracisternly injected 3H-metatonin and its distribution in the brain of the male Sprague-Dawley rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melatonin injected intracisternally is rapidly metabolized, and that the rate of its metabolism is accelerated by exposure to constant light or constant dark.
the brain is a site of rapid metabolism for melatonin, but that the hypothalamus is the most likely site of its synthesis and release.
the intracerebroventricularly injected 3H-metatonin disappeared very rapidly and was metabolized extensively in rat brain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intracisternal melatonin is cleared very rapidly from the cerebrospinal fluid and that it is taken up very rapidly by the brain, but that it is cleared from the brain even more rapidly.
melatonin is rapidly cleared from the cerebrospinal fluid of the brain.
intracisternal melatonin is rapidly metabolized in the brain and that melatonin is a very short-lived substance in this organ.
The main takeaway from our work is that
melatonin is a very rapidly metabolized substance in brain, and that its turnover rate in brain is not significantly different from that of the rest of the body.
the brain has a high affinity for melatonin and a very high turnover rate, and that melatonin is metabolized very rapidly in brain, probably in situ.
the brain has a very high metabolic capacity to metabolize intracisternally administered melatonin, and this is true even when the pineal gland is not functioning.
